title: Operation Niagara: five-day Toronto sprint by regulators, police and crypto firms to stop wallet-draining fraud
date_note: The Globe and Mail page shows only 'Published 2 hours ago' and says the sprint ran for five days last week; the publication day is used.
geo_basis: Sprint hosted at the offices of the Ontario Securities Commission, Toronto, per the Globe and Mail
summary: The Globe and Mail reports that Operation Niagara, a five-day sprint last week hosted at the Ontario Securities Commission, brought police, securities regulators and crypto firms together to stop criminals draining cryptocurrency wallets. Investigators uncovered nearly 1,500 compromised wallets, and approximately $5.7-million in wallet holdings were protected from theft, according to the article.
plain: Canadian and US agencies and crypto companies spent five days working together to protect compromised crypto wallets from being emptied, the Globe and Mail reports.
exec: Regulators and exchanges are coordinating in real time against wallet-draining fraud, per the Globe and Mail.

evidence.quote: This time around, investigators uncovered nearly 1,500 compromised wallets.
Approximately $5.7-million in wallet holdings were protected from theft

validation.note: Only the Globe and Mail read; the OSC's own release answered 403.
